Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet: Aurelius - capacity tradeoffs and asks

Camila — skimmed the attachment. Quick take: 60 reserved GPU-hours/day is doable but depends on the slot type. If they want low-latency (<=150ms p95) for interactive inference, we should be sizing for 4x the steady-state token throughput they listed to avoid queueing during bursts.

Options:
- Conservative: 60 reserved + 40% burst credit (cheaper CAPEX pressure, slightly higher OpEx).
- Aggressive: 90 reserved (higher commit) with smaller burst buffer — reduces tail-latency risk and simplifies infra.

I’m looping Laura to give a costed breakdown against our slot types. Also flagging that if we use quantized models aggressively we can shave ~25% GPU hours but should surface quality tradeoffs.

—Ben
Senior TPM, Capacity Planning
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet: Aurelius - capacity tradeoffs and asks

Ben/Camila — attached a short cost sheet (Drive link) and two slot mixes that balance latency vs cost:

Plan A (latency-priority): 3 x low-latency reserved slots (n1), 30 reserved hours/day per slot = ~90 reserved hours/day total. Estimated incremental monthly commit: $58k.
Plan B (cost-priority): 2 x mid-packed reserved slots (n2) + 40% burst pool = ~65 reserved hours/day equivalent. Estimated cost: $38k/month plus expected burst spend.

Notes:
- Quantization profile Q2 reduces GPU-hours ~22% but our internal eval flagged a 3-5% drop on edge-case completions for Aurelius’s use-case (sensitive for their search reranking flows).
- If Aurelius wants a guaranteed p95 latency <200ms we should prefer Plan A.

Drive cost breakdown: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FleetPlanningShared (see file: Aurelius_cost_matrix_v2.xlsx)

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Finance

Quick infra note:
- Region: their production should be hosted in us-west-2 to keep network hop low. We can mirror logs to eu-west-1 if needed for compliance.
- SLA: we can offer 99.5% uptime for dedicated slots; full latency SLOs require canary deployments and warm KV cache preloads — that adds ~2-4% to billed GPU time during warm periods.
- Operational ask: INFRA-1487 (work item) to ensure burst pool eligibility and automatic fallback to quantized variant if latency spikes. I’ve added the ticket to our sprint; ETA for readiness: 3 weeks from approval.

If Sales wants Plan A we’ll need sign-off by Jul 20 to meet Aug 2 start.

Karthik

Thanks, Camila/Laura — we reviewed both plans with our engineering and finance teams. Two clarifying Qs:

1) Is Plan B guaranteed to maintain 95% of median latency compared to Plan A, or will we see variable tails?
2) If we take Plan B, what is the expected incremental cost if we hit +40% burst for two weeks (approx. worst-case in our early trial)?

We prefer Plan B to minimize upfront commitment, but will consider Plan A if you can provide a small pilot-era SLA (latency guard rails) and a clearer burst-to-cost cap. Also attaching our internal MA summary (aurelius_ma_plan.pdf).

Best,

Bethany — thanks for the quick review and the MA plan. Short answers and next steps: 

- Plan B latency: median should track within ~95% of Plan A on steady state; tail variability is the risk. We’ll provide a short latency-runbook and a nightly tail-report during pilot.
- Burst cost cap: finance proposed a soft cap model — if bursts exceed 40% for more than one week, we’ll pause burst routing and engage you to decide whether to convert some burst to reserved at a pre-negotiated uplift (see HubSpot: https://hubspot.company.com/deals/DL-2026-119).

Action items:
1) Laura to produce the formal two-option quote by Jul 13 (Laura: please include a pilot-era SLA template).
2) Karthik to confirm INFRA-1487 timeline and include the warm-up hour estimate in the cost sheet by Jul 13.
3) Camila to run a 30-min sync with Aurelius + Finance on Jul 14 (proposed 10:00am PT) — calendar invite to follow.

I’ve attached the updated capacity tab and the Aurelius MA plan to the Drive folder (pipeline_capacity_request.xlsx, aurelius_ma_plan.pdf).

Thanks all — I’ll capture notes in HubSpot after the sync.
